sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A CONSIDERABLE/STRONG UPPER TROUGH BY LATE SPRING STANDARDS IS EXPECTED TO AMPLIFY/DIG EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD OVER THE GREAT BASIN TO THE CENTRAL/SOUTHERN ROCKIES BY TONIGHT. DOWNSTREAM OF THIS AMPLIFYING UPPER TROUGH...SHORTWAVE RIDING WILL OCCUR ACROSS THE MIDWEST TODAY...WITH A MODERATE BELT OF MID/UPPER WESTERLIES OTHERWISE REMAINING FROM THE OH/TN VALLEYS TO THE CAROLINAS/MID-ATLANTIC SEABOARD. IN VICINITY OF AN EXTENSIVE/CONVECTIVELY AUGMENTED EFFECTIVE WEST-EAST FRONTAL ZONE...A RELATIVELY MOIST AIRMASS COLOCATED WITH STEEP LAPSE RATES/MODERATELY STRONG FLOW ALOFT WILL RESULT IN AN ACTIVE SEVERE WEATHER DAY FROM THE PLAINS TO THE APPALACHIANS/SOUTHEAST STATES.

sections.title: PLAINS TO THE MIDWEST/MS VALLEY
sections.text: AHEAD OF THE WESTERN STATES UPPER TROUGH...NUMERICAL GUIDANCE CONSENSUS SUGGESTS THAT A LEAD SHORTWAVE TROUGH/SPEED MAX WITH COINCIDENT ONSET OF LARGE SCALE HEIGHT FALLS WILL REACH THE ROCKIES FRONT RANGE/CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS RELATIVELY EARLY THIS AFTERNOON. AS THIS OCCURS...APPRECIABLE SOUTH-CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS SURFACE CYCLOGENESIS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO A CONTINUED MOIST INFLUX ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS IN VICINITY OF A SHARPENING WEST-EAST ORIENTED FRONTAL ZONE. GIVEN THE AFOREMENTIONED LARGE SCALE SCENARIO...DEEP CONVECTION IS EXPECTED TO INITIALLY INCREASE THROUGH EARLY/MID AFTERNOON NEAR THE CO/WY FRONT RANGE INTO THE ADJACENT CENTRAL/NORTHERN HIGH PLAINS...WITH ADDITIONAL/MORE WIDESPREAD DEEP CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT PROBABLE BY MID/LATE AFTERNOON ACROSS NEB/FAR NORTHERN KS IN VICINITY OF THE SURFACE FRONTAL ZONE AND ATTENDANT MOIST/VERY UNSTABLE BOUNDARY LAYER. STRONG INSTABILITY/CONSIDERABLY VEERING WIND PROFILES WILL BE HIGHLY SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELLS ESPECIALLY ACROSS MUCH OF NEB AND ADJACENT PORTIONS OF NORTHERN KS/SOUTHERN SD/NORTHEAST CO. VERY LARGE HAIL WILL BE THE PRIMARY HAZARDS...BUT TORNADOES WILL BE POSSIBLE AS WELL GIVEN A RELATIVELY MOIST BOUNDARY/SUFFICIENT LOW LEVE

sections.title: OK/SOUTHERN KS TO NORTHWEST/WEST TX
sections.text: VERY HOT TEMPERATURES WELL INTO THE 100S AND STRONG MIXING WILL OCCUR IN VICINITY OF THE DRYLINE EXTENDING FROM SOUTHERN KS/WEST-CENTRAL OK SOUTHWESTWARD TO PORTIONS OF NORTHWEST/WEST TX THIS AFTERNOON. AIDED BY WEAK LATE DAY HEIGHT FALLS...ISOLATED TO SCATTERED SEVERE TSTMS ARE LIKELY TO DEVELOP BY LATE AFTERNOON ESPECIALLY ACROSS FAR SOUTHERN KS/WEST-CENTRAL OK/NORTHWEST TX. THIS WILL INCLUDE SOME SUPERCELLS GIVEN AMPLE INSTABILITY/DEEP LAYER SHEAR...WITH SEVERE HAIL AND DAMAGING DOWNBURSTS POSSIBLE. AT LEAST MODEST LINEAR-TYPE ORGANIZATION COULD OCCUR DURING THE EARLY EVENING WITH AN ENHANCED WIND THREAT GIVEN THE LAPSE RATES/DOWNDRAFT POTENTIAL AND A RELATIVE WEAKNESS IN MID TO HIGH LEVEL FLOW. BUT OTHERWISE...THE SEVERE THREAT SHOULD WANE IN INTENSITY THROUGH MID/LATE EVENING.

sections.title: TN/LOWER OH VALLEYS TO THE SOUTHEAST/MID-ATLANTIC STATES
sections.text: IT SEEMS LIKELY THAT AN MCS WILL BE ONGOING ACROSS THE LOWER OH/TN VALLEY AREA EARLY THIS MORNING. WHILE AN EARLY DAY SEVERE THREAT MAY REMAIN POSSIBLE ON AN ISOLATED BASIS...CURRENT THINKING IS THAT A COLD POOL/POTENTIAL MCV REMNANTS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO AN UPSWING IN STRONG/SEVERE TSTMS WITHIN A MOIST/UNSTABLE AIRMASS FROM THE TN VALLEY AND SOUTHERN/MIDDLE APPALACHIANS VICINITIES TO THE CAROLINAS/VA THIS AFTERNOON. SOME INITIAL MODAL SUPERCELLS WILL BE POSSIBLE...BUT ORGANIZATION INTO SEVERAL EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD PROPAGATING CLUSTERS ARE LIKELY TO OCCUR THROUGH THE AFTERNOON/EVENING...WITH DAMAGING WINDS AND SOME SEVERE HAIL POSSIBLE. IF CONFIDENCE INCREASES IN A PREFERRED CORRIDOR FOR WIND DAMAGE...WHICH IS AT LEAST SOMEWHAT DEPENDENT ON OVERNIGHT/EARLY MORNING CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENTS ACROSS THE LOWER OH/TN VALLEYS...A MODERATE RISK MAY NEED TO BE CONSIDERED FOR PORTIONS OF THE REGION. ..GUYER/GRAMS.. 06/19/2011

sections.title: CENTRAL PLAINS
sections.text: BY LATE AFTERNOON...A WARM FRONT WILL EXTEND ACROSS NORTHERN KS INTO SOUTHWEST IA/NORTHWEST MO. EASTERLY LOW LEVEL WINDS NORTH OF THE WARM FRONT WILL HELP TO TRANSPORT RICH MOISTURE WESTWARD...WITH DEWPOINTS WELL INTO THE 60S EXPECTED FROM CENTRAL NEB INTO PARTS OF IA/MO. LATEST OPERATIONAL AND MESOSCALE MODEL GUIDANCE SUGGESTS THAT STORMS WILL FIRST FORM ALONG THE FOOTHILLS OF THE ROCKIES FROM NORTHERN CO INTO SOUTHEAST WY. THIS ACTIVITY WILL SPREAD EASTWARD INTO PARTS OF WESTERN NEB AND NORTHWEST KS DURING THE EARLY EVENING. OTHER STORMS WILL LIKELY FORM BY 00Z ALONG THE SURFACE WARM FRONT AND DRIFT EASTWARD. VERTICAL SHEAR PROFILES IN THIS ENTIRE REGION WILL SUPPORT SUPERCELLULAR STRUCTURES CAPABLE OF VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. IT APPEARS THE BEST THREAT FOR TORNADOES WOULD BE IN REGION OF HIGH DEWPOINTS AND BACKED LOW LEVEL WINDS NORTH OF THE WARM FRONT. DURING THE EVENING...STORMS MAY CONGEAL ACROSS NEB INTO A LINEAR MCS. THIS ACTIVITY WOULD THEN SPREAD EASTWARD INTO PARTS OF IA/MO WITH A RISK OF WIDESPREAD DAMAGING WINDS.

sections.title: OH VALLEY INTO CAROLINAS
sections.text: A LARGE BOW ECHO COMPLEX IS AFFECTING PARTS OF IND/KY THIS MORNING. THESE STORMS ARE MOVING GENERALLY EASTWARD INTO AN AREA OF PRECIPITATION...WHERE MORE STABLE CONDITIONS SHOULD RESULT IN SLOW CONVECTIVE WEAKENING. NEVERTHELESS...THE SOUTHERN FLANK OF THIS ACTIVITY WILL TRACK SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS MIDDLE/EASTERN TN THROUGH MIDDAY...AND EVENTUALLY INTO PARTS OF VA/NC/SC/GA THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. PRESENT INDICATIONS ARE THAT STORMS WILL RE-INTENSIFY BY LATE MORNING AND AFFECT THIS REGION WITH ANOTHER ROUND OF DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL.

sections.title: OK/TX
sections.text: THE SURFACE DRYLINE IS EXPECTED TO EXTEND FROM WESTERN OK INTO WEST TX BY LATE AFTERNOON. HOT SURFACE TEMPERATURES AND STEEP LOW LEVEL LAPSE RATES ALONG AND WEST OF THE DRYLINE...COUPLED WITH AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OF 1500-2000 J/KG RANGE EAST OF THE DRYLINE...WILL PROMOTE ISOLATED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT. THE STORMS THAT FORM WILL LIKELY REMAIN WITHIN A FEW COUNTIES OF INITIATION DUE TO INCREASING INHIBITION FARTHER EAST. HOWEVER...THOSE STORMS THAT DO FORM WILL POSE A RISK OF DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL. ..HART/ROGERS.. 06/19/2011

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: UNSEASONABLY STRONG TROUGH DIGGING SEWD ACROSS INTERMOUNTAIN REGION TO SRN ROCKIES BY TONIGHT. DOWNSTREAM ANOTHER MCV HAS DEVELOPED OVERNIGHT FROM MCS ACTIVITY AND CURRENTLY MOVING EWD OH VALLEY TO REACH THE MID ATLANTIC COAST LATER TONIGHT. SURFACE LOW WILL DEEPEN CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON/TONIGHT WITH APPROACHING STRONG UPPER TROUGH. E/W WARM FRONT CENTRAL PLAINS WILL SHIFT NWD TO VICINITY NEB/KS BORDER THIS AFTERNOON AND BE A PRIMARY FOCUS FOR THE EXPECTED SEVERE THUNDERSTORM OUTBREAK BEGINNING LATER THIS AFTERNOON AND TONIGHT. DRY LINE WILL AGAIN BECOME ACTIVE LATE THIS AFTERNOON FROM WRN OK INTO W CENTRAL TX WHERE VERY HOT/STEEP LAPSE RATES WILL RESIDE ALONG WITH MORE THAN SUFFICIENT INSTABILITY TO FUEL PULSE STORM DEVELOPMENT.

sections.title: CENTRAL PLAINS
sections.text: ONLY ADJUSTMENTS TO THE MDT RISK WAS TO INCLUDE A LITTLE MORE OF NERN CO AS VEERING WIND PROFILES ON THE N SIDE OF DEEPENING SURFACE LOW ALONG WITH MLCAPES AOA 1500 J/KG FAVOR SUPERCELLS WITH VERY LARGE HAIL POTENTIAL. ADDITIONALLY TORNADOES WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH ANY SUPERCELL THAT DEVELOPS. FURTHER E THE AIR MASS VICINITY E/W WARM FRONT BECOMES VERY UNSTABLE WITH MLCAPES RANGING UPWARDS TO 3-4000 J/KG ACROSS NRN KS/SRN NEB. CAP WILL WEAKEN SUFFICIENTLY BY LATE AFTERNOON TO ALLOW RAPID DEVELOPMENT OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS INCLUDING SUPERCELLS. ALONG WITH VERY LARGE HAIL...TORNADOES WILL BE POSSIBLE...PARTICULARLY ALONG AND JUST N OF WARM FRONT WHERE BACKED SURFACE FLOW WILL ENHANCE THE SHEAR. DURING THE EVENING...STORMS ARE LIKELY TO DEVELOP UPSCALE INTO A FORWARD PROPAGATING MCS ACROSS NEB. THIS ACTIVITY WOULD THEN SPREAD EASTWARD INTO PARTS OF IA/MO WITH A THREAT OF WIDESPREAD DAMAGING WINDS.

sections.title: LWR OH/TN VALLEYS INTO CAROLINAS
sections.text: IMPRESSIVE MCV DEVELOPED OVERNIGHT AND CURRENTLY MOVING EWD ACROSS IND. A BAND OF STRONG WESTERLIES DEVELOPED S OF MCV AND WILL PROVIDE FAVORABLE SHEAR FOR REDEVELOPMENT OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON FROM TN VALLEY EWD TO MID ATLANTIC STATES BY TONIGHT. AIR MASS CURRENTLY RECOVERING FROM W TO E ACROSS TN VALLEY IN THE WAKE OF MORNING MCS AND BY EARLY AFTERNOON WILL BECOME MDTLY UNSTABLE WITH MLCAPES AOA 2000 J/KG EWD ACROSS TN VALLEY AND SRN APPALACHIANS. THUNDERSTORMS WILL INCREASE RAPIDLY BY MID AFTERNOON AND FORM INTO LINE SEGMENTS/BOWS GIVEN THE 40-50KT OF WLY SHEAR ACROSS TN VALLEY. WIND DAMAGE WILL BE THE PRIMARY THREAT AS STORMS CONTINUE TO DEVELOP UPSCALE AS THEY SPREAD EWD ACROSS TN VALLEY TO CAROLINAS. ADDITIONAL SEVERE STORMS POSSIBLE BY MID AFTERNOON FURTHER S INTO NRN GA WHERE AIR MASS BECOMES MDTLY UNSTABLE WITH SOMEWHAT WEAKER SHEAR THAN FURTHER N.

sections.title: OK/TX
sections.text: THE SURFACE DRYLINE IS EXPECTED TO EXTEND FROM WESTERN OK INTO WEST TX BY LATE AFTERNOON. HOT SURFACE TEMPERATURES AND STEEP LOW LEVEL LAPSE RATES ALONG AND WEST OF THE DRYLINE...COUPLED WITH AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OF 1500-2000 J/KG RANGE EAST OF THE DRYLINE...WILL PROMOTE ISOLATED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT. THE STORMS THAT FORM WILL LIKELY REMAIN WITHIN A FEW COUNTIES OF INITIATION DUE TO INCREASING INHIBITION FARTHER EAST. HOWEVER WITH NEAR DRY ADIABATIC LAPSE RATES TO 500MB...MLCAPES AOA 2000 J/KG AS WELL AS DCAPE TO ALMOST 2000 J/KG...STORMS THAT DO FORM WILL POSE A RISK OF DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL. ..HALES/HURLBUT.. 06/19/2011

sections.title: THERE IS A MDT RISK OF SVR TSTMS FROM NERN CO INTO NEB
sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS FROM THE CENTRAL PLAINS ESEWD ACROSS THE MIDDLE MS VALLEY INTO THE CAROLINAS...

sections.title: NERN CO INTO NEB
sections.text: A LOW LEVEL BOUNDARY EXTENDS FROM NORTH CENTRAL NEB SWWD INTO NERN CO WHERE A DEN CYCLONE/VORTICITY ZONE IS EVIDENT FROM SURFACE DATA. TO THE SE OF THIS CONVERGENCE ZONE...MOIST SELY LOW LEVEL FLOW CONTINUES FROM NRN KS ACROSS NEB INTO NERN CO. A SMALL CLUSTER OF STRONG/SEVERE STORMS HAS DEVELOPED NEAR THE BOUNDARY NEAR THE CO/NEB/WY BORDER INTERSECTION...AND ADDITIONAL CONVECTION IS LIKELY TO DEVELOP WITHIN THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS NEAR THE SURFACE BOUNDARY. SWLY WINDS ALOFT ARE EXPECTED TO GRADUALLY INCREASE INTO TONIGHT IN ADVANCE OF THE UPSTREAM UPPER LOW OVER THE GREAT BASIN...MAINTAINING STRONG VERTICAL SHEAR OVER THE REGION WHERE MODERATELY STEEP LAPSE RATES ARE ENHANCING INSTABILITY WITH MLCAPE OF 1500-2500 J/KG. THIS WILL SUPPORT AN INCREASE IN SEVERE STORM POTENTIAL AS CONVECTION MOVES NEWD INTO THE PLAINS THIS EVENING WITH A THREAT FOR VERY LARGE HAIL...A FEW TORNADOES AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS. STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO GROW UPSCALE INTO ONE OR TWO BOWING MCS/S TONIGHT IN RESPONSE TO A STRENGTHENING NOCTURNAL LOW LEVEL JET...WITH THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREAT TRANSITIONING TO DAMAGING WIND GUSTS ALONG THE LEADING EDGE OF THE MCS OUTFLOW. sections.title: PLAINS TO THE MIDWEST/MIDDLE MS VALLEY
sections.text: SHARPENING FRONTAL ZONE EARLY THIS EVENING EXTENDS GENERAL WEST-EAST FROM NEAR THE NORTHERN KS/SOUTHERN NEB BORDER TO THE LOWER/MIDDLE MO VALLEY. REGIONAL 00Z OBSERVED RAOBS SAMPLE A MOIST/HIGHLY UNSTABLE AIRMASS AS PER 00Z LBF/OAX/TOP/DVN/ILX SOUNDINGS. SUPERCELL AND ASSOCIATED LARGE HAIL/TORNADO THREAT WILL CONTINUE ESPECIALLY ACROSS WESTERN NEB/FAR NORTHEAST CO...AS WELL AS NORTHEAST KS/ADJACENT MO VALLEY VICINITY THROUGH MID EVENING. SUBSEQUENT UPSCALE MCS-TYPE DEVELOPMENT/ORGANIZATION SEEMS HIGHLY PROBABLE ACROSS NEB...WITH FORWARD PROPAGATION LIKELY TO YIELD AN INCREASING DAMAGING WIND THREAT LATER THIS EVENING/OVERNIGHT AMID STRENGTHENING LOW LEVEL EASTERLIES. ADDITIONAL STORMS ARE LIKELY TO INCREASE/EXPAND NORTH OF THE WARM FRONT FROM NORTHEAST KS/FAR SOUTHEAST NEB INTO WESTERN/SOUTHERN IA AND NORTHERN MO THROUGH LATE EVENING...WITH AN INITIAL LARGE HAIL THREAT AND PERHAPS MCS DEVELOPMENT WITH AN INCREASING WIND THREAT WITH AID OF A DRAMATICALLY STRENGTHENING SOUTHWESTERLY LOW LEVEL JET.

sections.title: TN VALLEY/SOUTHERN APPALACHIANS/CAROLINAS
sections.text: EARLY/MID EVENING ONGOING STORMS /INCLUDING A SUPERCELL OR TWO/ WILL LIKELY PERSIST AT LEAST FOR SEVERAL MORE HOURS...WITH AID FROM A VERY UNSTABLE FEED AS PER THE 00Z NASHVILLE OBSERVED RAOB. IT IS NOT ENTIRELY CLEAR AS TO WHETHER THESE STORMS WILL PERSIST EAST OF THE APPALACHIANS...BUT AN ISOLATED SEVERE HAIL/WIND THREAT CANNOT BE RULED OUT LATE THIS EVENING/OVERNIGHT ESPECIALLY IF UPSTREAM STORM EXPANSION/ORGANIZATION CONTINUES TO OCCUR. ..GUYER.. 06/20/2011
